title: Friday
style: cinematic horror film still, dramatic moody lighting with the subject clearly visible and centered, small snowbound American river town in deep winter, a vintage walnut shortwave radio with a warm amber dial glowing against cold blue night, film grain, 35mm, highly detailed, subject clearly visible, no text, no watermark
caption:
Final part. She unplugged it. It kept talking. 📻

Original fiction. New series tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: Last time: the radio read Lena's obituary for Friday night, and a familiar whisper told her to pull the plug.
scenes.image: the old walnut radio glowing on a kitchen table, a full moon in the frosted window behind it

scenes.narration: Friday, six o'clock. She knelt behind the walnut case and yanked the cord from the wall. The dial went dark.
scenes.image: woman kneeling behind an antique radio pulling a cloth power cord from the wall, dark kitchen

scenes.narration: She sat on the kitchen floor and waited. The clock ticked. The furnace hummed. Nine. Ten. Eleven.
scenes.image: woman sitting on a kitchen floor with her back against the cabinets, moonlight across the tiles

scenes.narration: At two minutes to midnight, the dial began to glow. The plug was lying in her lap.
scenes.image: an unplugged antique radio glowing amber anyway, its cloth cord coiled on the floor

scenes.narration: Good evening, Millbrook. But it wasn't the announcer. It was older. Rougher. And the kitchen filled with the smell of pipe tobacco and peppermint.
scenes.image: wisps of pipe smoke curling in front of a glowing radio dial in a dark kitchen

scenes.narration: Hello, sweetheart. It's Grandpa. There's no obituary. I read it myself. It was the only way to make you stop listening.
scenes.image: a framed photograph of a smiling old man on a shelf beside the radio, lit by its amber glow

scenes.narration: I listened for fifty years. Every life I saved, it took one back. And at the end, it took me. I won't let it have you too.
scenes.image: an empty worn armchair beside a snowy window, a pipe resting on the armrest

scenes.narration: Put me in the attic, Lena. Leave the plug out. And whatever you hear up there, don't come up.
scenes.image: narrow wooden attic stairs disappearing into darkness, a faint amber glow at the top

scenes.narration: She did. But some nights, through the ceiling, she still hears him. Reading tomorrow. To someone else. The radio doesn't need you to listen. It only needs somebody.
scenes.image: a woman lying awake in bed staring at the ceiling, a thin line of amber light through the floorboards above

scenes.narration: Tomorrow night, a new series. A night-school teacher meets the substitute nobody hired.
scenes.image: an empty night-school classroom lit by flickering fluorescent lights, a man in a grey suit at the chalkboard
